title: FAR U2·W2 — Accounting for Income Taxes (ASC 740) (CPA Core · from CMA m11)
lessonHtml:
Cold open — book income and taxable income are not the same number

MBG depreciates equipment one way for the books and a faster way for taxes (the CMA month 11 tax shield). That difference does not vanish — it creates a deferred tax. ASC 740 reconciles the financial statements to the tax return by recognizing the future tax consequences of today's differences. This is consistently one of FAR's hardest and most-tested areas.

Income tax expense has two parts

Total income tax expense = current tax expense + deferred tax expense. Current is the tax actually payable on this year's taxable income. Deferred is the change in deferred tax assets and liabilities arising from temporary differences that will reverse in future periods.

Temporary versus permanent differences

Temporary differences arise when an item hits the books and the tax return in different periods; they reverse over time and create deferred taxes:

  • A taxable temporary difference (taxable later) creates a deferred tax liability (DTL) — e.g., tax depreciation exceeding book depreciation now.
  • A deductible temporary difference (deductible later) creates a deferred tax asset (DTA) — e.g., a warranty accrued for books but deducted for tax only when paid, or unearned revenue taxed when received.

Permanent differences never reverse and create no deferred tax — they only change the effective tax rate. Examples: tax-exempt municipal bond interest, fines and penalties, and the nondeductible portion of certain expenses.

Worked deferred tax

Illustrative, tying to Unit 1: in year 1, book (straight-line) depreciation is $80,000 while tax depreciation is $176,000. Tax depreciation exceeds book by $96,000 — a taxable temporary difference. At an enacted future rate of 24%, the deferred tax liability = $96,000 × 24% = $23,040. In later years book depreciation will exceed tax depreciation and the DTL reverses back toward zero. Deferred taxes are always measured at the enacted rate expected when the difference reverses — not the current rate if a change is already enacted.

Valuation allowance

A deferred tax asset is recognized in full, then reduced by a valuation allowance if it is more likely than not (greater than 50% probability) that some portion will not be realized — for instance, if future taxable income may be insufficient to use a deductible difference or a net operating loss carryforward. The allowance is a contra-asset that lowers the net DTA, and it is reassessed each period.

CMA bridge

CMA month 11 used the depreciation tax shield as a cash flow; FAR explains the financial-statement counterpart — the deferred tax liability the faster tax depreciation creates. The $96,000 book-versus-tax gap there is the temporary difference here.

Practice and recap

  1. Split tax expense into current and deferred.
  2. Classify a difference as temporary (creates deferred tax) or permanent (no deferred tax).
  3. Tax depreciation > book → DTL; warranty/unearned revenue → DTA.
  4. Measure deferred taxes at the enacted future rate; reduce a DTA by a valuation allowance when more likely than not unrealizable.

Recap: ASC 740 recognizes the future tax effects of temporary differences — the $96,000 excess of tax over book depreciation creates a $23,040 deferred tax liability at 24% — while permanent differences only move the effective rate and a valuation allowance trims a DTA that is more likely than not unrealizable.

flashcards.back: Current tax expense + deferred tax expense.
Deferred tax liability (DTL) — e.g., tax depreciation exceeding book depreciation.
Deferred tax asset (DTA) — e.g., accrued warranty or unearned revenue.

flashcards.front: Do permanent differences create deferred tax?
flashcards.back: No; they never reverse and only change the effective tax rate.

flashcards.front: At what rate are deferred taxes measured?
flashcards.back: The enacted tax rate expected when the temporary difference reverses.

flashcards.front: When is a valuation allowance recorded?
flashcards.back: When it is more likely than not (>50%) that part of a DTA will not be realized.

choices: Current tax expense + deferred tax expense
questions.explain: Tax expense combines the current payable and the change in deferred taxes.

questions.q: Tax depreciation exceeding book depreciation in the current year creates a:
questions.explain: A taxable temporary difference (taxable later) creates a deferred tax liability.

questions.q: Tax depreciation $176,000, book depreciation $80,000, enacted rate 24%. The deferred tax liability is:
Which is a PERMANENT difference (no deferred tax)?
questions.explain: Municipal interest never reverses; it is permanent and affects only the effective rate.

questions.q: A deferred tax asset is reduced by a valuation allowance when:
choices: It is certain to be realized
It is more likely than not that some will NOT be realized
questions.explain: A valuation allowance applies when realization of part of the DTA is more likely than not to fail.

questions.q: Deferred taxes are measured using the:
choices: Enacted rate expected when the difference reverses
questions.explain: Use the enacted future rate expected at reversal.

questions.q: An accrued warranty liability deducted for tax only when paid creates a:
questions.explain: It is a deductible temporary difference (deducted later) — a deferred tax asset.
